In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Commentary on Surat Yunus

It is a Meccan surah except for three verses, namely His words, exalted is He, ﴿If you are in doubt about what We have sent down to you﴾ up to the end of the three verses.

It is related from Muhammad ibn Sirin that he said: this surah came after the preceding surah.

His words, exalted is He, ﴿Alif, Lam, Ra﴾. Abu al-Duha related from Ibn Abbas that he said: ﴿Alif, Lam, Ra﴾ means: "I am Allah, the All-Seeing." He also related from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that he said: Ra, Ha, Mim, and Nun are the completion of the name al-Rahman.

Regarding the disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'at), there are opinions which we have mentioned at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah.

His words: ﴿These are the verses of the Book﴾. Abu Ubaydah said: its meaning is "these are the verses of the Book." The poet said:

(Those are my horses from it, and those are my mounts... their young are yellow like raisins)

Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning of the verse is: the verses which I sent down to you earlier are ﴿these are the verses of the Book, the Wise﴾. The Book is the Qur'an, and the Wise (al-Hakim) is the one made firm (al-Muhkam), according to the view of most exegetes; it is fa'il in the sense of maf'al, like His words: ﴿This is what is ready (ʿatid) with me﴾, meaning: prepared (mu'tad). Some of them said: al-Hakim is in its original form, and the Qur'an was named wise because it is like one who speaks with wisdom.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 2:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Is it a wonder for mankind?﴾ The ʿajab (wonder, astonishment): a state that overtakes a person upon seeing something contrary to the usual course.

The occasion of revelation of this verse: when Allah, exalted is He, sent Muhammad (ﷺ), the polytheists said: "Did Allah not find a prophet other than an orphan of Abu Talib?" So Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse, which is His saying: ﴿Is it a wonder for mankind?﴾ Its meaning: "Is it a wonder for people, i.e., the polytheists, ﴿that We have revealed to a man from among them﴾." The "man" here is the Prophet. As for His saying ﴿from among them﴾, they said its meaning is: he is a man whom they know by his name and lineage, who does not write, does not compose poetry, does not practice soothsaying, and does not lie.

As for His saying ﴿that he should warn mankind﴾: al-Indhar (warning) is informing together with frightening. As for His saying ﴿and give good news to those who have believed﴾, we have already explained the meaning of al-bushra (good tidings). As for His saying ﴿that they will have a true standing (qadam sidq) with their Lord﴾, there are four opinions concerning it:

The first opinion - and this is the view of the majority - is that qadam sidq is the righteous deeds. It is said: "So-and-so has a qadam (standing, precedence) in bravery, and a qadam in knowledge." And it is said: "So-and-so placed his foot (qadam) in such-and-such," when he begins it by his action.

The second opinion: that qadam sidq is the reward.

The third opinion: it is reported from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: qadam sidq is happiness in the first decree (al-dhikr al-awwal).

The fourth opinion: that what is meant by it is the Messenger, and "qadam sidq" means a true intercessor (shafiʿ sidq); this was said by Muqatil ibn Hayyan.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿The disbelievers said: Indeed, this is clearly a magician.﴾ It has been recited in two readings: "lasaahirun mubin" (a clear magician) and "inna hadha lasihrun mubin" (indeed, this is clear magic). So "the magician" refers to the Messenger, and "magic" refers to the Qur'an.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 3:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days﴾. Regarding "days" there are two opinions:

One of them: they are like the days of the Hereafter, each day being a thousand years. The other: they are like the days of this world.

His saying: ﴿Then He istawa (rose) over the Throne﴾. We have already explained the position of the People of the Sunnah regarding istiwa', which is that we affirm it and entrust its knowledge to Allah, Exalted is He, without interpretation (ta'wil) and without explanation (tafsir).

As for the Mu'tazilah, they interpreted istiwa' as istila' (domination, seizure), and this is invalid according to the scholars of the Arabic language.

It is related from Ahmad ibn Abi Du'ad, who was one of the leaders of the Mu'tazilah, that he said to Ibn al-A'rabi: "Do the Arabs know istiwa' in the sense of istila'?" He said: "No." It is also related that this question came up in the assembly of al-Ma'mun, and Bishr al-Marisi said: "Istiwa' means istila'." Abu al-Samra' — a man from among the people of the language — said to him: "You have erred, O shaykh; the Arabs do not know istila' except after a prior inability."

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿He arranges the affair﴾. Mujahid said: He decrees the affair. ﴿There is no intercessor except after His permission﴾. Its meaning: intercessors do not intercede except with His permission. This is a refutation of al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, for he used to say: "On the Day of Resurrection, al-Lat and al-'Uzza will intercede for me."

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿That is Allah, your Lord﴾, meaning: that One who did this is your Lord. ﴿So worship Him. Will you not remember?﴾ Will you not take heed?

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 4:

The words of His Exalted Saying, ﴿To Him is your return, all of you. The promise of Allah is true﴾: "promise of Allah" is in the accusative, meaning: Allah promised a true promise. ﴿Indeed, He originates creation and then repeats it﴾: its meaning is known. ﴿That He may reward those who believed and did righteous deeds with justice﴾: Ibn 'Abbas said: "with justice" means with equity (al-'adl). ﴿And those who disbelieved will have a drink of scalding water﴾: al-hamim is the water whose heat has reached its extreme. In the stories (al-qasas) it is related that the Fire has been kindled against it since the day it was created until the disbelievers enter [into] (1) the Fire. His saying: {And a painful punishment because they used to} i.e., a painful, agonizing punishment for their disbelief.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 5:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿It is He who made the sun a shining radiance and the moon a light﴾ – the verse. The sun and the moon are two luminous bodies, one of them brighter than the other. His saying ﴿made the sun a shining radiance﴾ means: possessing radiance; ﴿and the moon a light﴾ means: possessing light. His saying ﴿and determined for it stages﴾ – some of them said: this refers to the moon specifically, and others said: it refers to both of them, except that He suffices with mentioning one of them over the other.

The stations (manazil) of the moon are twenty-eight stations, whose names are known among the Arabs. Fourteen of them are always visible, and fourteen of them are always hidden; whenever one rises, one sets, and the moon descends into one of them each night.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿that you may know the number of years and the reckoning﴾ means: He determined it in stages so that you may know the number of years and the reckoning of months and days. His saying ﴿Allah did not create that except with truth﴾ means: for the truth.

His saying: ﴿He details the signs for a people who know﴾ – its meaning is clear.

Al-Sam'ani's commentary on Surah 10, verse 6:

His words, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, in the alternation of the night and the day﴾. Its meaning is known, up to the end of the verse, and we have mentioned it before.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 7:

The Exalted's saying: ﴿Indeed, those who do not expect meeting Us﴾. His saying "do not expect" (la yarjūn) has two interpretations:

One of them: they do not fear. The other: they do not hope.

His saying ﴿meeting Us﴾ has already been explained earlier. His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿and are content with the worldly life﴾. Qatadah said: they seek it and rejoice in it. His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿and are at rest in it﴾ means they settle into it. His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿and those who are heedless of Our signs﴾. Heedlessness (al-ghaflah) is a forgetfulness that afflicts the heart and turns it away from the awareness of knowledge.
Then he said: ﴿Those—their abode is the Fire because of what they used to earn.﴾ Its meaning is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 9:

His Exalted saying: ﴿Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - their Lord will guide them by their faith﴾. Mujahid said: this is the meaning of His Exalted saying: ﴿a light by which he walks﴾. Others said: "Their Lord will guide them" means: their Lord will guide them by their faith to Paradise. ﴿Rivers will flow beneath them﴾, meaning: beneath the trees. His saying: ﴿in Gardens of Bliss﴾.

Then He said: ﴿Their call therein will be﴾ meaning: their supplication therein. ﴿"Glory be to You, O Allah"﴾. This is a phrase of glorifying and declaring God free of any imperfection.

It is reported in the traditions that the saying ﴿"Glory be to You, O Allah"﴾ is a sign between the people of Paradise and the servants. When they wish for food, they say, "Glory be to You, O Allah," and then the servants enter with the dishes. Every dish is a mile by a mile, its legs are of pearls, and upon every dish there are seventy thousand platters, and in every platter there is a kind of food that does not resemble the others. Then birds come like the camels of Bakht (Bactrian camels), their legs of one color, their wings of one color, and their bellies and backs of one color, and they alight before the people of Paradise, and they eat from them whatever they wish. Then they fly away as they were.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And their greeting therein will be peace﴾, meaning: the greeting among them to one another will be with peace. It is also said that its meaning is: the greeting of the angels to them is with peace. And it is said: the greeting of God to them is with peace.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the last of their call will be﴾ meaning: the last of their saying: ﴿"Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds"﴾. So the beginning of their affair is glorification, and the end of their affair is praise and gratitude.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 11:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if Allah were to hasten for people the evil [consequence] as they hasten [for] the good﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: This refers to the statement of a man who, in anger, says to his family and children: "May Allah curse you, may Allah not bless you." Its meaning: "If Allah were to hasten for people the evil," that is, the disliked [outcome], "as they hasten for the good," that is, as they desire to be given the good quickly. ﴿He would have decreed for them their term﴾, so they would all perish and die. And His saying: ﴿So We leave those who do not expect meeting Us﴾, that is, who do not fear meeting Us, ﴿in their transgression﴾, that is, in their misguidance. His saying ﴿wandering blindly (ya'mahun)﴾: they vacillate; and it has been said: they persist excessively.

The report from the Prophet (ﷺ) is also established that he said: "O Allah, I am a human being; I become angry as human beings become angry. So whichever [man] I have insulted or cursed, make it for him a purification and a mercy." And on this subject there are many reports, all of them sound.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 12:

The Most High's saying ﴿And when harm touches man﴾, i.e., adversity, ﴿he calls upon Us, lying on his side, or sitting, or standing﴾. The people of tafsir said: this admits of two meanings.

One of them: when harm touches man, he calls upon Us whether lying on his side, or sitting, or standing.

The other: it admits of: when harm touches man, he calls upon Us, lying on his side, or sitting, or standing, meaning: in all of these states.

The Most High's saying: ﴿But when We remove from him his harm, he passes on﴾. In it there are two meanings:

One of them: he passes on being a transgressor as he was before. The other: he continues in what he was before. Some of them said regarding this meaning:

(As if the youth had never been bare when he is clothed, and had never been a pauper when he has become wealthy.)

The Most High's saying: ﴿as if he had never called upon Us against a harm that touched him﴾: its meaning is, as if he had never asked Us to remove the harm that touched him. His saying ﴿Thus the deeds of the extravagant have been made attractive to them﴾. Ibn Jurayj said: thus were made attractive to the extravagant ﴿what they used to do﴾ of supplication at the time of trial, and neglect of gratitude in times of ease. And there is another meaning in it: that just as your deeds were made attractive to you, so likewise were the deeds of the extravagant who were before you made attractive to them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 13:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We had already destroyed generations before you when they wronged, and their messengers came to them with clear proofs﴾. Its meaning is known. And His saying: ﴿and they would not have been [such as] to believe﴾. Al-Zajjaj (al-Zajjaj, the grammarian) said: this refers to a people whom God knew would not believe. And Ibn al-Anbari said: God prevented them from faith as a recompense for their disbelief. His saying: ﴿Thus do We recompense the criminal people﴾. This is evidence that the statement of Ibn al-Anbari is more correct.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 14:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Then We made you successors (khalā'if) in the land after them﴾ mean: successors (khulafa') in the land after them. ﴿That We may see how you act﴾ means: that He may test you, so that He sees how you act.

It is narrated from ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "O son of Umm ʿUmar, you have been made a successor, so see how you act."

It is also narrated that he said in his sermon: "O believers, indeed Allah has made you successors so that He may see how you act. So show Allah your good deeds, and refrain from ugly deeds."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 15:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who do not expect to meet Us say, "Bring us a Quran other than this, or change it."﴾ It is related in the books of tafsir (exegesis) that the polytheists said to the Prophet: "O Muhammad, if you wish us to believe in you, then bring a Quran in which there is no reviling of our gods, and in which there is no mention of the Resurrection and the Rising. And if God has not sent it down like this, then say it from yourself." So God, exalted is He, revealed this verse.

If someone says: What is the difference between His saying ﴿Bring a Quran other than this﴾ and His saying ﴿or change it﴾? Are their meanings not one and the same? The answer: Their meanings differ. His saying ﴿Bring a Quran other than this﴾ permits that he bring another alongside it, whereas His saying ﴿or change it﴾ can only mean that he abandon this and bring something else.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say, "It is not for me to change it on my own accord. I only follow what is revealed to me. Indeed I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day."﴾ Its meaning is well known, and it is as if He said: "I did not say this from my own accord, so that I would say something else from my own accord."

Then He said: ﴿Say: "If God had willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made you aware of it."﴾ That is, if God had willed, He would not have sent down the Qur'an upon me. ﴿Nor would He have made you aware of it﴾ means: nor would God have informed you of it. ﴿I have already lived among you a lifetime before it.﴾ The word ʿumr and the word ʿumr (with a different vowel pattern) have the same meaning. The poet said:

(Youth has departed and the years have failed me... and friends and time have changed toward me.)

The length of the lifetime he lived among them before it is forty years, by the consensus of the scholars ('ahl al-'ilm). For the Prophet (ﷺ) was sent to them when he was forty years old, and he remained in Mecca for thirteen years, and in Medina for ten, and he died at the age of sixty-three. In a report from Anas: "The Prophet (ﷺ) stayed in Mecca for ten years and in Medina for ten years, and God took him at the age of sixty." The first report is more apparent and better known.

His saying ﴿Will you not then use your reason?﴾ means: "Will you not then understand?" (tafaqquh)

Almost-complete passage: the commentary on Q. 10:17 is brief. Translating it per the instructions.

On His the Exalted's words: ﴿Who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah or denies His signs? Indeed, the criminals will not succeed.﴾ Its meaning is well known.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 18:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And they worship besides Allah that which neither harms them nor benefits them﴾. If someone says: How does He say ﴿nor harms them﴾ when there is no doubt that it did harm them?

The answer regarding this: its meaning is that it does not harm them if they abandon its worship, and it does not benefit them if they worship it. And His statement: ﴿And they say, "These are our intercessors with Allah"﴾. If someone says: How did they say, "These are our intercessors with Allah," when they did not believe in the Resurrection?

The answer: They used to say, "These are our intercessors with Allah concerning the affairs of our livelihood in this world."

And His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Say, "Do you inform Allah of what He does not know in the heavens or on the earth?"﴾ That is: Do you inform Allah? ﴿Exalted is He above what they associate with Him﴾ — its meaning is well known.

The reality of the verse is: a refutation and a denunciation of them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 19:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And mankind was not but one community﴾ have two interpretations.

The first: the view of Mujahid, which is that people were upon Islam (islam) in the time of Adam until one of his two sons killed the other, ﴿and then they differed﴾.

The second view: that the Arabs were upon the religion of Ibrahim (Abraham) until they differed. It is well known that the first of the Arabs to change the religion of Ibrahim was Amr ibn Luhayy. And it is established that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I saw [Amr] ibn Luhayy dragging his intestines in the Fire."

It is also said regarding the verse that the intended "community" is the people of Noah's ark, peace be upon him.

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord﴾ mean: concerning the postponement and respite; ﴿the matter would have been decided between them concerning that wherein they differ﴾ meaning: judgment would have been passed between them concerning that wherein they differ.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 20:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They say, "Why has no sign been sent down to him from his Lord?"﴾ If someone says: "Did the Messenger not already bring signs, according to your claim?"

The answer to this: Yes. And the meaning of the verse is: "Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord, of the kind we propose?"

﴿So say, "The unseen belongs only to Allah."﴾ That is: knowledge of the unseen belongs to Allah. If He wills, He brings the sign you ask for, and if He wills, He does not bring it. ﴿So wait, and I am with you among those who wait.﴾ That is: wait for the unseen; indeed I am with you among those who wait.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 21:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when We let people taste mercy after adversity has touched them﴾. Al-dhawq (tasting) is taking into the mouth something that has a taste, so that one may find its taste. As for mercy here, there are two opinions:

One of them: it is well-being (al-'afiyah). The other: it is abundance (al-khisb) and blessing (al-ni'mah).

As for al-darra' (adversity), there are two opinions:

One of them: it is hardship (al-shiddah). The other: it is drought and famine (al-jadb wal-qahat).

﴿Touched them﴾ means: it reached them.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then they have a scheme against Our signs﴾. Al-makr (scheming) is turning a thing away from its proper course by means of trickery. Mujahid said: ﴿They have a scheme against Our signs﴾ means denial and mockery.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Allah is swifter in planning﴾, meaning: swifter in seizing. It is also said: its meaning is that the punishment that comes from Him is swifter in destroying you than what you do in repelling the truth and denying it.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed Our messengers record what you plot﴾, its meaning is well known.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 22:

The saying of Allah Most High: ﴿It is He who enables you to travel on land and sea﴾. It has been recited in two ways: "yusayyirukum" (yusayyirukum) and "yunshirukum" (yunshirukum). The well-known reading is "yusayyirukum," and its meaning is: facilitating the path of travel for you on land and sea. As for the one who recites "yunshirukum," its meaning is: He scatters you (yubaththukum). It is narrated from al-Dahhak that he said: "The sea is the cities (al-amsar), and the land is the desert (al-bawadi)." And the saying of Allah Most High: ﴿until, when you are in the ships﴾. The people of linguistics (ahl al-lughah) said: al-fulk (the ship) is used both as feminine and masculine. Allah Most High said: ﴿in the laden ship﴾ (al-fulk al-mashhun), and here He said: ﴿and they sail with them﴾. They also said: al-fulk may be used with the meaning of the singular and with the meaning of the plural. And His saying: ﴿with a fair wind﴾ means: gentle and mild.

It has been narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The wind is from the Mercy (rawh) of Allah. So ask Allah for its good, and seek refuge in Allah from its evil."

If someone says: How does He say: ﴿until, when you are in the ships and they sail with them﴾? Is this not a change of the speech from its direction?

The answer to this: The Arabs use the状 of witnessing (al-mu'ayanah) in place of address (al-mukhatabah), and address in place of witnessing. The poet said:

(Wa-shattat mazar al-'ashiqin fa-asbahat ... 'asiran 'ala talabika ibnat Makhram)

Some said: the meaning of the verse is: until, when you are in the ships and they sail with them with a fair wind, O Muhammad. And His saying: ﴿and they rejoice in it, a violent wind comes upon them﴾, which is the severe, destructive one. The poet said:

(Fi fayliqin shahba' mulmumah ... ta'simu bil-hasir wal-dari'

And His saying: ﴿and the waves come upon them from every place﴾. The mawj (waves): that which appears on the sea from the wind.

﴿And the waves come upon them from every place, and they think that they are encompassed, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion: "If You deliver us from this, we will surely be among the thankful."﴾

And His saying: ﴿and they thought﴾, and were certain, ﴿that they were encompassed﴾. It is said of one who is in affliction and hardship: he has been encompassed. And His saying: ﴿they called upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾ means: they were sincere in supplication, and called upon no one other than Allah. And His saying: ﴿"If You deliver us from this, we will surely be among the thankful"﴾, its meaning is well known.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So when He saved them, behold, they were insolent in the earth without right.﴾ Al-baghy (insolence/transgression): it is the intention to exalt oneself over others through injustice. Al-baghy here means corruption (fasad). It is said: "al-jurh baghā" (the wound became corrupt/festered) when it led to corruption, and "baghat al-mar'ah" (the woman committed adultery) when she committed fornication.

It has been narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Allah does not delay the one who commits baghy," meaning: He does not give him respite. And in the reports also: "Baghy is a hastening (musara'ah)" [a sudden, quick fall/consequence].

Then He said: ﴿O mankind, your insolence is only against yourselves.﴾ That is, the consequence (wabal) of your insolence falls upon you.

His words ﴿the enjoyment of the life of this world⦆ — it has been read as "matā'u l-ḥayāti l-dunyā" (with raf', nominative) and also as "matā'a l-ḥayāti l-dunyā" (with naṣb, accusative). Whoever reads it with raf' means: "It is the enjoyment of the life of this world." Whoever reads it with naṣb means: "You enjoy the enjoyment of the life of this world." It is reported from al-A'mash that he said: "al-matā' is the provision of the traveller." The scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ānī) said: the true meaning of the verse is that insolence is the enjoyment of the life of this world.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿Then to Us is your return, and We shall inform you of what you used to do.﴾ That is, We shall tell you of what you used to do.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 24:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, the example of the worldly life﴾ means: indeed, the description of the worldly life ﴿is like water which We sent down from the sky﴾, that is, from the clouds, ﴿and the plants of the earth mix with it﴾, meaning the rain mixes with the vegetation and the vegetation with the rain, ﴿from what men and livestock eat﴾. The meaning is clear. As for His saying: ﴿until, when the earth takes on its adornment (zukhruf) and is beautified﴾. Zukhruf is the perfection of beauty, and gold is called zukhruf because of its perfection in beauty. The meaning of zukhruf here is splendor and freshness. As for His saying: ﴿and is beautified﴾, that is, it adorned itself. They said its meaning is: it brought forth plants, bore fruit, and ripened.

As for His saying: ﴿and its people think they have power over it﴾, its meaning is: its people think they are able to harvest it, pick its fruit, and reap it. As for His saying: ﴿Then Our command comes upon it by night or by day﴾, that is, Our punishment comes upon it by night or by day. As for His saying: ﴿and We make it a harvested field (ḥaṣīd)﴾, the ḥaṣīd is the mowed, and the meaning here is total annihilation by punishment. As for His saying: ﴿as if it had not flourished yesterday﴾, Mujahid said: its meaning is, as if it had not been inhabited yesterday. Others said: as if it had not been standing yesterday. It is said: "Ghaniya fulan bil-makan" when he stood in it, and al-maghani are the dwellings. Labid said:

(And indeed I have grown weary of life and its length... and of asking these people how Labid is.)

(And I dwelt a sabt before the course of Dahis... if only the stubborn soul were given eternity.)

The meaning of ghaniytu is: I dwelt; and sabt here means the age (dahr).

Qatada said: the meaning of the verse is that one who clings to the world, the command of God and His punishment come upon him when he is most heedless and most pleased with it.

As for His saying: ﴿Thus We make the signs clear for a people who reflect﴾, its meaning is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 25:

The Exalted's saying: ﴿And God calls to the Abode of Peace﴾. It is reported in the traditions that the Prophet said: "There is no day on which the sun rises except that on its two sides there are two angels who make the creatures hear, except the two jinn and humankind: 'Come, hasten to your Lord!'" Then he recited the Exalted's saying: ﴿And God calls to the Abode of Peace﴾. Also in the narrations: "There is no day nor night except that a caller calls out: 'O seeker of good, come forward! And O seeker of evil, desist!'"

As for the Abode of Peace: the "abode" is Paradise. Regarding "peace" (al-salam) there are two opinions:

The first: that it is God Himself. The second: that al-salam means safety (al-salamah), as if He said: He calls to the Abode of Peace, from calamities.

Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Baqir related, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah al-Ansari, may God be pleased with them both, that the Prophet said: "I saw in my dream as if Jibril was at my head and Mika'il was at my feet. One of them said to his companion: 'Strike a parable for him.' The other said: 'Your likeness, O Muhammad, is that of a king who built a house, then built within the house a chamber, then placed in the chamber a feast, then invited the people to it. Some of them abandoned it and some of them responded. The king is God the Exalted, the house is Islam, the chamber is Paradise, and the caller is you. Whoever responds enters Islam, and whoever enters Islam eats from it.'"

As for His saying: ﴿And He guides whom He wills to a straight path﴾: the straight path is Islam. There are other opinions regarding it, which we have mentioned earlier.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 26:

The Most High's saying: ﴿For those who do good is the best [reward] and more﴾. Al-ihsan (doing good) here means Islam, and al-ihsan is the utterance "There is no god but Allah." They differed regarding "the best [reward] and more." It is related from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, Ibn 'Abbas, Hudhayfah, Qatadah, and a group of the Successors (tabi'un) that they said: "the best" is Paradise, and "more" is looking upon Allah, exalted is He. Abu al-Qasim ibn Bint Mani' related, from Hudbah ibn Khalid, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Thabit, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Suhayb (may Allah be pleased with them), that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When the people of Paradise enter Paradise, Allah, the Most High, says: 'O people of Paradise, indeed you have a promise with Me, and I will fulfil it for you.' They say: 'And what is it? Did You not make our faces bright? Did You not make our scales heavy? Did You not admit us to Paradise and save us from the Fire?' He said: Then He will unveil Himself to them, and they will look upon His Face, and they will not have been given anything more beloved to them than looking at Him." Then he recited the Most High's saying: ﴿For those who do good is the best [reward] and more﴾.

﴿For those who do good is the best [reward] and more﴾

Imam Abu al-Muzaffar said: This hadith was related to us by Abu al-Husayn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Naqqur (with lightening of the letter) in Baghdad, who said: Abu al-Qasim ibn Habbabah related to us, who said: Abu al-Qasim ibn Bint Mani' related to us... the report, which Muslim recorded in his Sahih.

There are other opinions regarding the verse.

It is related from 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said: "The more" is a chamber of pearl having four thousand doors. It is related from al-Hasan al-Basri that he said: "The best" is the equivalent of reward, and "more" is the increase over the equivalent up to seven hundred times. Mujahid said: "The best" is the equivalent, and "more" is the good pleasure of Allah, the Most High.

The Most High's saying: ﴿And neither dust nor humiliation will cover their faces﴾. Al-qatr: the blackness of the face; and the root of al-qatar is smoke.

His saying: ﴿nor humiliation﴾, meaning: disgrace.

His saying: ﴿Those are the companions of Paradise; therein they will abide forever﴾. Its meaning is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 27:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And those who earned evil deeds, the recompense of an evil deed is its like﴾, to the end of the verse. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿And whoever brings an evil deed, they will not be recompensed except with its like﴾.

His words: ﴿Humiliation will cover them﴾ mean: humiliation will overwhelm them, i.e., disgrace. ﴿They will have no protector from Allah﴾ means: no preventer. And His words: ﴿As if their faces had been covered with pieces of the dark night﴾ are read with two readings: "qit'an" and "qit'an". The "qit'a" with the ṭā' vowelled (qiṭ‘an) is the plural of "qiṭ‘a" (a piece), and "qat'" with the ṭā' sukūn (qaṭ‘an) is the singular.

If it is said: How is it that it did not say "qiṭ‘an min al-layl muẓlimah" (pieces of the night, dark)?

We say: The estimated sense of the verse is: pieces of the night in a state of its darkness. Thus have the lexicographers said.

﴿They are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever﴾ — apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 28:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And on the Day We gather them all together, then We will say to those who associated partners [with Allah], "Stay in your place, you and your partners."﴾ The verse. The meaning of the verse: Then We will say to those who associated partners [with Allah]: Remain, you and your partners, in your place.

His words: ﴿So We will separate them﴾. Its meaning: We will distinguish between them, i.e., We will divide between the polytheists and the idols. It is from the word zalla (to separate), not from the word dhalla (to be humiliated). ﴿And their partners will say, "You did not used to worship us."﴾ The "partners" are the idols that they made partners with Allah, the Most High, according to their own claim. And His words: ﴿You did not used to worship us﴾ mean: you used to worship us by our solicitation and our call.
God's saying, ﴿So God is sufficient as a witness between us and you; indeed, we were unaware of your worship.﴾ Its meaning is well known.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 30:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿There every soul will know [tabluu] what it has done﴾, the verse. It is recited with two readings: "tatlu" and "tabluu". As for His saying "tabluu", Mujahid said: it means "tukhtabar" (is tested), that is, it finds it and stands over it. As for His saying "tatlu", al-Akhfash said: it reads (yaqra'), so it carries the meaning of His saying: ﴿On the Day of Resurrection We will bring out for him a book which he will find spread open. "Read your record; sufficient is yourself against you this Day as a reckoner."﴾

The second view: the meaning of "tatlu" is "tattabi'" (follows). The poet said:

(I see the doubtful one following the doubtful, as I saw the wolf following the wolf)

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿every soul [will be repaid for] what it sent before﴾, meaning: what it had put forward. His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿and they will be returned to Allah, their true Master﴾. If someone says: He has said elsewhere: ﴿and that the disbelievers have no master﴾, and here He says: ﴿they will be returned to Allah, their true Master﴾, so how are the two verses reconciled?

The answer to this: the "mawla" there means the helper and protector, and the "mawla" here means the owner, so there is no contradiction between the two verses.

His saying [may He be exalted]: ﴿and what they used to fabricate will be lost to them﴾, meaning: what they used to lie about will be gone from them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 31:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth?﴾ Provision from the heaven is by rain, and from the earth by plants. His saying: ﴿Or who controls hearing and sight?﴾ its meaning: and who gave you hearing and sight? His saying ﴿And who brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living?﴾ its meaning: and who brings the sperm-drop out of the living, and the living out of the sperm-drop, the ear of grain out of the seed, and the seed out of the ear of grain, the chick out of the egg and the bird out of the egg, the tree out of the date-stone, and the date-stone out of the tree, the believer out of the disbeliever, and the disbeliever out of the believer.

His saying ﴿And who arranges the affair?﴾ means: and who decrees the affair? His saying: ﴿They will say, "Allah." So say, "Will you not then fear Him?"﴾ its meaning: will you not then fear shirk (associating partners with Allah) despite this acknowledgment?

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 32:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So that is Allah, your true Lord﴾. Its meaning: So that One whose attribute is this is your true Lord. And His saying: ﴿So what is there after the truth except error?﴾ Its meaning: So what is there after the truth except falsehood?

It is related from Harmalah that he said: I asked (Malik ibn Anas) about singing (ghina'), and he recited this verse: ﴿So what is there after the truth except error?﴾

It is related from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, one of the Tabi'un, something close to this in this meaning. And His saying ﴿Then how are you turned away?﴾ means: How is it that you are diverted from the path of truth?

Allah's saying: ﴿Thus has the word of your Lord been justified﴾, meaning: it became obligatory. ﴿The word of your Lord﴾, meaning: the decree of your Lord. ﴿Against those who defied﴾, meaning: those who disbelieved, ﴿that they will not believe﴾. The people of tafsir said: this refers to particular groups of people whom Allah knew would not believe.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 34:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: Is there any of your associates who originates creation and then repeats it?﴾ Its meaning: who brings creation into being and then repeats it. And His saying: ﴿Say: God originates creation and then repeats it﴾ means: He brings creation into being and then repeats it. The meaning of "repetition" (al-i'adah) is the reviving for resurrection on the Day of Judgment. And His saying ﴿So how are you turned away?﴾ means: how are you diverted?

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 35:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Is there any of your associates who guides to the truth? Say: Allah guides to the truth.﴾ Its meaning is clear. And His saying: ﴿Is one who guides to the truth more worthy to be followed, or one who does not find guidance unless he is guided? So what is wrong with you? How do you judge?﴾ It has been recited in many readings. The people of Arabic grammar (ahl al-'Arabiyya) said: the soundest of them is "amman la yahiddi" or "yahiddi," in the form of idgham (assimilation), because its meaning is "yahtadi" (he is guided). Then He said: ﴿unless he is guided﴾. If it is said: how does He say ﴿unless he is guided﴾ when it is not conceivable of idols that they be guided or that they be guiding? The answer is in two respects:

The first: the meaning of guidance (hidayah) here is transport (naql), meaning: it does not move from place to place unless it is moved.

The second respect: this is mentioned in a figurative manner (majaz), for the polytheists believed about the idols that they hear, understand and guide. So He mentioned that about the idols in accordance with what they believed, and placed them in the position of one who understands in this address, and affirmed their inability to guide. His saying: ﴿So what is wrong with you? How do you judge?﴾ Its meaning is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 36:

His, the Exalted and Glorified, saying: ﴿And most of them follow nothing but conjecture﴾ to the end of the verse. Ẓann (conjecture): a state between doubt (shakk) and certainty (yaqīn). And His saying: ﴿Indeed, conjecture avails nothing against the truth﴾ means: conjecture can in no way take the place of the truth. And His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do﴾ its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 37:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And this Qur'an could not have been fabricated by other than Allah﴾, the verse, and in it there are two meanings:

One of them: And this Qur'an could not be a fabrication from other than Allah.

The second meaning: And it is not fitting for the likes of this Qur'an that it be fabricated by other than Allah, based on His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And it is not for a Prophet to deceive﴾, meaning: it is not fitting for the likes of a Prophet to deceive.

And His saying: ﴿But it is a confirmation of what was before it﴾ has two views:

One of them: a confirmation of what was before it of the Torah and the Gospel.

The second: a confirmation of the thing which the Qur'an has before it, namely the Resurrection and the raising up.

And His saying: ﴿And a detailed explanation of the Book, about which there is no doubt, from the Lord of the worlds﴾. Tafsil (detailed explanation) means clarification (tabyin), and the meaning of the rest of the verse is known.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 38:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"? Say, "Then bring a surah like it."﴾ The meaning of the verse: it is an argument against the disbelievers by means of the miracle of the Qur'an. For they used to say, "Muhammad has invented it," so He said to them: If he invented it and brought it from his own self, then you bring a like of it.

If it is said: He said, ﴿Then bring a surah like it,﴾ so is there a "like" of the Qur'an from which a surah may be brought?

The answer: its meaning is, "Bring a surah of the like of it in eloquence, composition and soundness of meaning." It was also said: its meaning is, "Bring a surah like a surah of the Qur'an."

As for His saying: ﴿And call upon whomever you can besides God﴾, its meaning is: seek help from whomever you can besides God ﴿if you are truthful.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 39:

His saying: ﴿Nay, they denied that which they did not encompass in knowledge of it﴾. Al-ihata (comprehensive encompassing) with regard to the knowledge of a thing is: knowing it from all its aspects. The meaning of the verse is: Nay, they denied the Qur'an and did not encompass its knowledge, meaning: they did not know it.

And His saying: ﴿And its interpretation (ta'wil) had not yet come to them﴾. That is: its interpretation had not come to them, and its meaning is: they did not know what its outcome (ta'wil) would lead to, the final result of their affair. Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Thus did those before them deny; so see how was the end of the wrongdoers﴾. The apparent meaning is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 40:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And among them are those who believe in it, and among them are those who do not believe in it. And your Lord is most knowing of the corrupters.﴾ Its meaning: among them are those who believe in it—in the Qur'an—like the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) from among the Emigrants (muhajirun) and the Helpers (ansar). And among them are those who do not believe in it, like Abu Jahl and whoever followed him. And among them, some said: among them are those who believe in it both secretly and openly, like the sincere believers, and among them are those who do not believe in it secretly, like the hypocrites.

﴿And your Lord is most knowing of the corrupters.﴾ Its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 41:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if they deny you, then say: "For me is my deed, and for you is your deed"﴾, the verse. Its meaning: for me is my deed and its recompense, and for you is your deed and its recompense. His saying: ﴿You are free of what I do, and I am free of what you do﴾ is like His saying: ﴿For you is your religion, and for me is my religion﴾, and like His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 42:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And among them are those who listen to you﴾ up to the end of the verse. Al-istima' (listening) means seeking to hear. They would seek to hear the Qur'an in order to refute and deny it, not to understand it and believe in it. As for His saying: ﴿Can you make the deaf hear?﴾ al-summ (deafness) is an affliction that prevents hearing. What is meant by deafness here is deafness of the heart, for when they did not listen to the Qur'an in order to believe in it and accept it, it was as if they had not listened at all, and He placed them in the position of the deaf. Al-summ is the plural of al-asamm (the deaf). Al-Zajjaj said: They were indeed hearing in the literal sense, but due to the intensity of their hatred and enmity toward the Prophet (ﷺ), they did not listen in order to understand, so He made them as though they had not heard. As for His saying: ﴿Even though they do not use reason﴾, its meaning is: even though they were ignorant.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 43:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And among them are those who look at you﴾. Naẓar (looking) is seeking sight by turning the eye; as for naẓar al-qalb (the looking of the heart), it is seeking knowledge through reflection (fikrah). His saying: ﴿Will you, then, guide the blind?﴾ He made them like the blind, because they did not look in order to seek the truth. The meaning of blindness here is blindness of the heart. Some have said: He made them like the blind just as He made them like the deaf, since they benefited neither with their hearing nor with their sight.

Ibn al-Anbari, quoting from Ibn Qutaybah, mentioned that he used this verse as evidence that hearing is superior to sight, for God, exalted is He, said of deafness: ﴿If they used to not reason﴾, and said of blindness: ﴿And if they used to not see﴾.

Ibn al-Anbari said: This is an error, because the intended meaning of the verse is blindness of the heart, not blindness of the eye, and likewise deafness of the heart, not deafness of the ear. On this basis, no preference arises.

Ibn al-Anbari said: Also, the sense of sight is superior to the sense of hearing. Do you not see that beauty in it is greater, and the loss from its absence is greater? The Messenger (ﷺ) called the two of them the "two precious things" of a person, for he said: "God, exalted is He, says: Whoever I take his two precious things and he is patient and seeks reward, he will have no recompense but Paradise."

When a man is blind, he cannot see his advance from his retreat, nor the path of his error from the path of his rectitude, and he becomes a captive within himself, and the general benefits of his limbs are rendered inoperative for him.
Allah's saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong the people at all, but the people wrong themselves.﴾ Its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 45:

His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿And the Day He gathers them, [it will seem] as if they had not remained but an hour of the day﴾. The meaning of the verse: bringing close the time of their death to the time of their resurrection. This is like His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿As if they had not remained but an hour of a day﴾. And His saying: ﴿They will recognize one another among themselves﴾ means: some of them will recognize one another. In some reports: a person on the Day of Resurrection recognizes the one beside him, but does not speak to him out of awe and dread. And His saying: ﴿Those who denied the meeting with Allah have certainly lost, and they were not guided﴾. Here, "loss" (khusran) means the loss of the self (nafs), and there is nothing greater than the loss of the self. In some reports: "O son of Adam, you are in the house of trade, so profit within it with your self."

"The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And whether We show you some of what We promise them﴾. Mujahid said: "Some of what We promise them" is: the killing on the day of Badr. Others said: the meaning of the verse is: "Whether We punish them during your lifetime, or We take you (in death) before their punishment," ﴿then to Us is their return﴾, and their return is to Us. And His saying: ﴿then Allah is Witness over what they do﴾ is clear in meaning, and "thumma" (then) here is in the sense of "wa" (and).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 47:

The Most High's saying: ﴿And for every nation there is a messenger﴾. The ummah (nation) is the community when they are upon one method and one aim. The rasul (messenger) is everyone who bears a message to deliver it with truth. The Most High's saying: ﴿So when their messenger comes﴾. Mujahid said: "So when their messenger comes, as a witness over them on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿he judges between them with justice﴾, that is, with fairness, ﴿and they will not be wronged﴾, meaning: nothing of their right will be diminished."

There is another meaning in the verse: that the meaning of His saying, ﴿So when their messenger comes﴾, is: when their messenger comes with warning and admonition, he judges between them with justice, that is, with truth. Its meaning is that before the coming of the messengers, no reward or punishment is due.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 48:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they say, "When is this promise, if you are truthful?"﴾ He means: the promise of the Hour.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say: I possess no power to benefit or harm myself, except as Allah wills﴾ — the verse. Al-mulk (possession, dominion): a power by which one disposes of a thing. His words ﴿harm nor benefit﴾ mean: repelling a harm or bringing about a benefit that Allah, exalted is He, has not decreed.

His words ﴿For every nation there is a term (ajal)﴾ — al-ajal (the term, appointed time): a fixed period set for the arrival of a matter.

His words ﴿When their term comes, they cannot delay it by an hour, nor can they advance it﴾ — the meaning is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 50:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Say: Tell me, if His punishment comes upon you by night or by day﴾. Al-bayat (bayat) is that which occurs at night.

And His words: ﴿What is it that the criminals seek to hasten of it?﴾ Its meaning: What is it that the criminals seek to hasten from Allah? It has also been said: What is it that the criminals seek to hasten from the punishment? The real meaning is that they used to seek to hasten the punishment, like the statement of al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, for he said: "O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky, or bring us a painful punishment." Then Allah the Exalted said in this verse: ﴿What is it that the criminals seek to hasten of it?﴾, meaning: What do the criminals know of what they seek to hasten and request? It is like a man saying to another: "What have you done to yourself?" when he has done something ugly.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 51:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Then, when it befalls, will you believe in it?﴾ It has been said in the tafsir: the meaning of His words "then" (ʾa-thumma, "then/after that") is: there, when it befalls, that is, the punishment, ﴿will you believe in it?﴾ meaning: will you believe in Allah? Who has the punishment befallen? That is, descended. Then He said: ﴿Now?﴾ and there is an ellipsis in it, and its meaning is: now you believe in it, ﴿while you used to seek to hasten it﴾ in denial and mockery.
Almighty Allah's statement: ﴿Then it will be said to those who did wrong, "Taste the punishment of eternity. Are you being recompensed except for what you used to earn?"﴾ The meaning is apparent.

"His saying, the Exalted: ﴿They ask you to inform them, "Is it true?"﴾ means: they ask you for information, "Is it true?" Al-haqq (the truth) is the opposite of al-batil (falsehood), and it is said: al-haqq is that which is established by proof. His saying: ﴿Say, "Yes, by my Lord, it is surely true, and you cannot escape [it]."﴾ means: Say, "Yes, by my Lord." ﴿Indeed, it is true, and you cannot frustrate [Allah].﴾ means: and you will not escape the punishment, because whoever is unable to achieve something has been deprived of it."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 54:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if every soul that had wronged had everything on earth, it would surely offer it as ransom﴾. Al-iftida' (ransoming) here means giving up whatever one can be saved by from the punishment. His saying: ﴿And they will conceal their regret when they see the punishment﴾ has two opinions:

The first: the saying of Abu 'Ubayda (Ma'mar ibn al-Muthanna), which is that its meaning is: they will show their regret.

The second opinion: the leaders among them will conceal the regret from the weak (followers), out of fear of their blame and reproach.

His saying: ﴿And it will be judged between them with justice, and they will not be wronged﴾. We have already explained its meaning.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 55:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth.﴾ If someone says: Do you not hold that the heavens are seven and the earths are seven? Then how does He mention "the heavens" in the plural form and "the earth" in the singular form (al-wuhdan)?

The answer: The singular here carries the sense of the plural, and the Arabs sometimes mention the singular with a plural form and the plural with a singular form. It has also been said: although the earths are seven, only this one earth is visible, while the rest are hidden, so it was mentioned in the singular form.

As for His words: ﴿Indeed, the promise of Allah is true, but most of them do not know.﴾ its meaning is apparent.
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿He gives life and causes death, and to Him you will be returned.﴾ Its meaning is well known.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 57:

Allah's words: ﴿O mankind, there has certainly come to you an admonition from your Lord﴾, to the end of the verse. The admonition (al-mawi'ah) is speech delivered in the manner of knowledge that leads to the betterment of the servants.

His words: ﴿and a healing for what is in the breasts﴾. The healing (al-shifa') here is the cure for the ailment of ignorance (al-jahl). The scholars have said: there is no ailment greater than ignorance, no remedy more precious than the remedy for ignorance, no physician more scarce than the physician of ignorance, and no cure more remote than the cure for ignorance.

As for His words ﴿what is in the breasts﴾: the breast (al-sadr) is the place of the heart, and it is the most precious place in the human being, because of its proximity to the heart.

His words: ﴿and guidance﴾, meaning: guidance away from misguidance. His words: ﴿and mercy for the believers﴾. Mercy (al-rahmah) is a bounty bestowed upon one in need. For if a king sent a gift to another king, it would not be said that he has shown him mercy, even though this is a bounty in reality, because he did not place it upon one in need.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 58:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Say: "In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy"﴾. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: The bounty of Allah is the Qur'an, and His mercy is Islam. It is also reported from some of them: The bounty of Allah is Islam, and His mercy is the Qur'an. It is reported from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: The bounty of Allah is the Qur'an, and His mercy is that He made us among its people. This is also related from Ikrimah.

His words: ﴿so let them rejoice﴾. Al-Hasan recited: "fa-bidhalika falatafrahu" (so let them rejoice), and its meaning is: so let them be amazed (fa-lat'ajjabu).

His words: ﴿It is better than what they accumulate﴾, that is, better than the dirhams and dinars that the disbelievers amass.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 59:

The Exalted's saying: ﴿Say: Have you considered what God has sent down to you of provision, and you made of it [some] unlawful and [some] lawful?﴾ The people of tafsir (exegesis) said: The meaning of this is the sawa'ib (free-roaming camels released for their gods) and the hawami (camels protected from burden or pasture after a set number of births) which the people of polytheism made unlawful for themselves. We have already mentioned this in the tafsir of Surat al-An'am, and what they made lawful and what they made unlawful [is mentioned] in the tafsir of His saying: ﴿And they say: What is in the wombs of these livestock is exclusively for our males and forbidden to our females﴾. If it is said: How does this meaning hold, when He says at the end of the verse: ﴿Say: Has God permitted you, or do you invent [lies] against God?﴾

The purpose of the verse is not interrogation; rather, its purpose is rebuttal and denunciation of them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 60:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And what do those who fabricate lies against Allah think will happen to them on the Day of Resurrection?﴾ They said: its meaning is: "And what do those who fabricate lies against Allah think will happen to them on the Day of Resurrection? Will good befall them, or will evil befall them?" The real meaning is that evil will befall them, because that is what suits their fabrication.

And His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah is full of bounty toward mankind, but most of them do not give thanks.﴾ In the exegetical works: "Out of a thousand, one is grateful."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 61:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And you are not engaged in any affair﴾. Sha'n (affair, matter): it is an indefinite noun, and it is like the saying of one person to another: "What has brought you (ma hamalaka)? What is your state (ma baluka)? What is your affair (ma sha'nuka)?" His saying ﴿in any affair﴾ means: in any of the affairs (shu'un).

His saying: ﴿And you do not recite from it any Qur'an﴾. If it is said: what is the meaning of His saying ﴿from it﴾, when the Qur'an has not been mentioned before? The answer to this has two aspects. One of them is that its meaning is: "And you do not recite from the affair any Qur'an." The other is that it refers back to the Qur'an as well: it is concealed (ubtin) in His saying ﴿from it﴾ and made manifest (uzhir) in His saying ﴿any Qur'an﴾, as a magnification of it. His saying ﴿and you do not do any deed except that We are witnesses over you﴾: al-shuhud (witnesses) here is the plural of shahid (witness).

His saying ﴿when you are immersed in it﴾: Ibn al-Anbari said: "idh tufidun" means "when you rush into it," and al-ifadah is the pushing forward through abundance. His saying ﴿And not absent from your Lord﴾ means: "and not hidden from your Lord ﴿of an atom's weight﴾," that is, of the weight of a dharrah. The dharrah is the small ant; it is also said that it is what appears in a ray of sunlight. The first is the well-known meaning.

His saying ﴿on the earth or in the heaven, nor anything smaller than that﴾ means: smaller than the dharrah. ﴿Nor greater﴾ means: nor anything greater than the dharrah, up to what none knows the extent of except Allah, may He be exalted. His saying ﴿except that it is in a clear Book﴾ means: except that He has it clearly recorded in the Book, meaning the Preserved Tablet.

In the well-known reports: "When Allah, may He be exalted, created the pen, He said: 'Write.' It said: 'What shall I write?' He said: 'Write what will occur until the Day of Resurrection.'" And it is established through the narration of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Allah decreed the decrees fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth." Muslim recorded it in his Sahih.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 62:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Verily, the friends of Allah﴾ — the scholars differed concerning the friends of Allah (awliya' Allah), in several opinions:

One of them: they are those who believe and were mindful of God (yattaquna).

The second: they are those who are content with the decree (al-qada'), who give thanks in times of ease, and who are patient in times of trial.

The third: they are those who love one another for the sake of God, may He be exalted.

Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Among the servants of Allah are servants who are not prophets, yet the prophets and the martyrs will envy them for their station with Allah." A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, who are they?" The Messenger said: "A people who love one another by the spirit of Allah, without ties of kinship that they maintain, nor wealth that they exchange. Indeed, upon their faces there is light, and they are upon pulpits of light. They do not fear when people fear, and they do not grieve when people grieve." Then he recited: ﴿Verily, the friends of Allah—no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve.﴾ Abu Dawud mentioned it in his Sunan, close to this wording.

The fourth: the friends of Allah are those who, when they are seen, [the remembrance of] Allah is recalled.

In some raised (marfu') reports from the Prophet: "He was asked: Who are the friends of Allah? He said: Those who, when they are seen, [the remembrance of] Allah is recalled." And in another narration: "Those who [remind] of Allah by their being seen."

As for His saying: ﴿no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve﴾ — fear (al-khawf) is a disturbance in the soul arising from the anticipation of something disliked, and grief (al-huzn) is a concern that settles in the heart due to some occurring cause.
His words, Exalted is He, ﴿Those who believed and were mindful of God﴾: the meaning is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 64:

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿For them is good news﴾. The scholars differed concerning this "good news," giving several opinions.

The first: Abu al-Darda' (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated from the Prophet that he said: "It is the good dream that a believer sees, or is shown."

And 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, Abu al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him), also narrated it.

It is also firmly established from the Prophet that he said: "The true dream is one part of forty-six parts of prophethood."

The second opinion: Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated from the Prophet: "As for the good news in the life of this world, it is the good praise, and in the Hereafter, it is Paradise."

The third: the good news is the descent of the angels of mercy bearing glad tidings from Allah, the Exalted, at the time of death.

The fourth: the good news is the believer's knowledge of his place in Paradise before he dies. This was said by a group of the Successors (tabi'un).

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿There is no change in the words of Allah﴾, its meaning is: there is no breaking of Allah's promise. And His saying: ﴿That is the supreme triumph﴾ means: the great salvation.

"His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And let not their speech grieve you﴾ — this is a complete pause (waqf tamm). Then He said: ﴿Indeed, all might (al-'izzah) belongs to Allah﴾, meaning: indeed, all victory (al-ghalabah) belongs to Allah. ﴿He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾ — its meaning is clear."

Qur'anic quotations: "Indeed, to Allah belongs whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth." Its meaning is known.

And His saying: "And those who call upon other than Allah do not follow partners." Its meaning: "And those who call upon other than Allah do not follow partners" in reality, because there is no partner for Allah. It was also said: its meaning is: "And those who call upon other than Allah do not follow partners" in knowledge and certainty; rather, they follow mere conjecture, as He said: "They follow nothing but conjecture, and they are only guessing." The meaning of His saying "yakhrusun" (they guess/lie) is: they lie, due to His saying: "Killed be the liars (al-kharrasun)," meaning: the liars.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 67:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He it is who made the night for you that you may rest therein﴾, its meaning is clear (ma'lum). His saying: ﴿and the day as something to see by﴾, i.e., making things visible (mubsiran) in it. It has also been said: its meaning is "and the day possessing sight (dha ibsar)", and this is like His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿in a life of good pleasure﴾, meaning "possessing pleasure" (dhat ridan). And His saying: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who listen﴾ is clear in meaning.

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 68:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They say, "Allah has taken a son." Glory be to Him!﴾ If someone says: What is the difference between taking a son and taking a khalil (intimate friend)?

The answer to this: The reality of khullah (intimate friendship) is restricted to Allah, may He be exalted, because khullah means the purification of affection, and this is permissible for Allah, may He be exalted. As for the reality of a son, it is not permissible for Allah, may He be exalted; so taking one is not permissible. Moreover, a person only takes a son in order that he may inherit his property, or in order to delight in him, or to help him with a matter, or to succeed him in his affairs, and Allah, may He be exalted, is far above all of this and it is not permissible for Him. Therefore, taking a son for Him is not permissible.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He is the Self-Sufficient (al-Ghani)﴾ is an indication of what we have said about the absence of need. His saying: ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. You have no authority for this﴾ means: you have no proof for this?

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Do you say about Allah what you do not know?﴾ its meaning is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 69:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: Indeed, those who invent lies against Allah will not succeed.﴾ That is: they will not be saved.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 70:

His saying ﴿A brief enjoyment in this world﴾ means: those who fabricate lies against Allah, their outcome is only a brief enjoyment in this world.

His saying: ﴿Then to Us is their return; then We will make them taste the severe punishment because they used to disbelieve﴾ — its meaning is well known.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 71:

The Most High's words: ﴿And recite to them the news of Noah﴾ mean: recite to them the report of Noah. ﴿When he said to his people: O my people, if my standing [among you] and my reminding [you] of the signs of Allah is burdensome to you﴾ means: if my standing [among you] is burdensome to you, that is, the length of my stay among you and my reminding [you]; and [my] warning you of the signs of Allah. ﴿Then in Allah have I put my trust﴾. They said: this is a parenthetical interjection (i'tiraḍ) in the speech and in the meaning. As for His words: ﴿So gather together your affair﴾, it is connected to what preceded, as if He said: if my standing [among you] and my reminding [you] of the signs of Allah is burdensome to you, then gather together your affair. In the irregular (shadh) reading: "fa-ajmi'ū amrakum" (فاجمعوا أمركم), which ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī recited.

His words: ﴿So gather together﴾. Al-Farrāʾ said: resolve upon your affair and call upon ﴿your partners﴾. Al-Zajjāj said: gather your affair together with your partners, except that, since the word "maʿa" (مع, "with") was dropped, the noun was put in the accusative (naṣb). The poet said:

(Would that I knew, while wishes do not benefit, until I see my affair and my affair gathered [resolved upon]...)

That is: resolved upon it. As for His words: ﴿Then let not your affair be a cause of doubt to you﴾, meaning: obscured (multabisan), and from it come "al-ghamām" (cloud) and "al-ghamm" (distress). As for the Most High's words: ﴿Then carry out [your decision] against me﴾, it was read in the irregular reading as "thumma afḍū ilayya" (ثم أفضوا إلي) with the fa', whereas the well-known reading has the qaf. Mujāhid said its meaning is: then know what is in your souls. It was also said its meaning is: turn toward me with killing and harm. This is by way of challenge (ta'jīz), for he spoke these words and they were unable to bring any harm upon him, so this was a kind of miracle (mu'jizah) for him. Others said: His words ﴿carry out [your decision] against me﴾ mean: then do what you are going to do, and act as you are going to act. This is like the words of the sorcerers: ﴿So decree what you will decree﴾, meaning: act as you will act. The true meaning of "qaḍāʾ" (decree) is the firm establishing of a matter and the completion of it, and from it one says of a man when he dies: "Qad qaḍā fulān," meaning: so-and-so has finished his affair.

His words, the Most High: ﴿And do not give me respite﴾, meaning: do not delay me.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 72:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿But if you turn away, then I have not asked you for any reward﴾. Its meaning: if you turn away, then I have not asked you for any reward (thawab) for conveying the message. His words: ﴿My reward is only from Allah﴾, i.e., my reward is only from Allah. ﴿And I have been commanded to be among the Muslims﴾, i.e., among the monotheists (al-muwahhidin). Some of them said: the meaning of His words ﴿among the Muslims﴾ is among those who submit (al-mustaslimin) to the command of Allah.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 73:

The Exalted said: ﴿So they denied him, and We saved him and those with him in the ark﴾. The people of tafsir (tafsir: exegesis of the Qur'an) said: There were eighty men with him in the ark. The first to be carried was the ant (dharra), and the last to be carried was the donkey (himar). Satan clung to the tail of the donkey, and he began to say, "Noah, to the donkey: enter!" and it would not enter, until he said: "Enter, O Satan!" So he entered, and Iblis was with him.

And the Exalted said: ﴿And We made them successors﴾, meaning: We made those who were with him in the ark the successors (khala'if) of the people whom We drowned in their homes, dwellings and abodes. And the Exalted said: ﴿And We drowned those who denied Our signs. So look how was the end of those who were warned﴾. Al-gharq (drowning): destruction by water; and al-ghamir (the one who submerges). It is said that the duration of the drowning was forty days, and from the time the water was sent down from the sky until the water receded (nadaba) was six months and some days.

"And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Then after him We sent messengers to their peoples, and they came to them with clear proofs﴾ — meaning: after Noah, [We sent] messengers to their peoples. ﴿But they were not going to believe in what they had denied before﴾ — meaning: they were not going to believe in what the people of Noah had denied before. ﴿Thus does Allah seal the hearts of the transgressors﴾ — meaning: He sets a seal upon the hearts of the transgressors."

**Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on Surah 10, verses 75–77:**

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿Then after them We sent Musa and Harun to Fir'awn and his chiefs with Our signs, but they acted arrogantly, and they were a guilty people﴾. Its meaning is clear. The verse that follows it is likewise of known meaning.

"The Almighty's words: ﴿They said: Have you come to us to turn us away from that which we found our fathers upon?﴾ Its meaning: to turn us away. Qatadah said: "to turn us away" means "to twist us" (latalwina), and Tha'lab, among the later scholars, said the same.

And His words: ﴿And that greatness may be yours in the land﴾. Mujahid said: al-Kibriya' (greatness) means kingship, and kingship was only called al-Kibriya' because it is the greatest thing sought in this world. It was also said: the meaning of al-Kibriya' is magnificence (al-'azamah). And it was said: its meaning is dominance (al-ghalabah).

His words: ﴿And we are not believers in you both﴾: that is, we are not those who confirm (bi-musaddiqin)."
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And Pharaoh said, "Bring me every learned sorcerer."﴾ In Surat al-Qasas it is mentioned that he gathered seventy thousand sorcerers.
"And His saying: ﴿So when the magicians came, Moses said to them, "Throw down what you are about to throw."﴾ That is: cast down what you are about to cast."

And His saying: ﴿So when they had cast, Moses said, "What you have brought is magic. Indeed, Allah will render it void. Indeed, Allah does not let the work of the corrupters succeed."﴾ The meaning of magic (sihr) has already been explained earlier. ﴿Indeed, Allah will render it void﴾ — i.e., He will make it go away. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not set right the work of the corrupters﴾ — its meaning is well known. It is related in the stories (al-qasas) that they were seventy thousand, each one of them with a rope and a staff. They cast those ropes and staffs, and they began to appear in the eyes of the people as if they were serpents and vipers.

The passage is short. Translating: "And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And Allah will establish the truth by His words﴾. Its meaning: Allah will raise the truth by His verses. ﴿Even though the criminals dislike it﴾."
