Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 83:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿But none believed in Moses except a few descendants (dhurriyyah) of his people﴾. Its meaning is: none believed in Moses except a few among his people. The scholars differed concerning the word dhurriyyah here. Some said: they were a people whose fathers were of the Copts (al-Qibt) and whose mothers were of the Children of Israel. Others said: they were a people who escaped the killing of Pharaoh, for when Pharaoh commanded that the sons of the Children of Israel be killed, a woman of the Children of Israel, whenever she gave birth to a son, would hand him over to a Coptic woman and say: "I have given him to you, out of fear for him of being killed." So those children grew up among the Copts, and they embraced Islam on that day, meaning the day of the magicians who were defeated. As for His saying: ﴿on [the basis of] fear of Pharaoh and their chiefs, lest he persecute them﴾, some of the scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: there is an ellipsis (hadhf) in the verse; it is as if He said: "on [the basis of] fear of the family of Pharaoh and their chiefs." This is like His saying: ﴿and ask the town﴾, meaning: the people of the town.

Among them are those who said: when Pharaoh was mentioned, his people entered with him, like a man who says: "The caliph or the governor has arrived with such-and-such," and the dwellings became too narrow for the people. Its meaning is: the caliph arrived and those who were with him.

Then He said: ﴿lest he persecute them﴾, meaning: lest he torment them. As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, Pharaoh was a tyrant (la'all) in the land﴾, meaning: a transgressor in the land, ﴿and indeed he was among the extravagant (al-musrifin)﴾, which is well known.

Almost the whole passage is quoted from tafsir; I translate it faithfully.

God the Exalted said: ﴿And Moses said, "O my people, if you have believed in God, then rely upon Him, if you are Muslims."﴾ Tawakkul (reliance): it is trust in God and depending upon Him in matters. And His saying: {if you are Muslims} means: if you are Muslims.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 85:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then they said, "In Allah have we put our trust."﴾ That is: in Allah we have relied. And His saying: ﴿Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people.﴾ Concerning this there are two opinions:

The first: "Do not destroy us at the hands of the wrongdoers, so that they are tried (by us) or think that we were not upon the truth." This was said by Abu Mijlaz.

The second: "Do not punish us with a punishment from You, so that they think they are better than us, and that becomes a trial for them."
And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And save us by Your mercy from the disbelieving people﴾. Its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 87:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We revealed to Moses and his brother, "Settle your people in Egypt in houses, and make your houses a qiblah, and establish prayer"﴾. The meaning of His saying ﴿tabawwa'a﴾ is "take (for yourselves)."

The poet said:

(We are the sons of 'Adnan, there is no doubt... honour and kingship were settled (taba'wa'a) by us)

As for His saying ﴿for your people in Egypt, houses, and make your houses a qiblah and establish the prayer﴾, the people of tafsir mentioned that Pharaoh ordered the churches and places of worship of the Children of Israel to be destroyed when Moses came and called him to God. So God, exalted is He, commanded them to instruct the Children of Israel to take mosques in their houses. This is the meaning of His saying ﴿and make your houses a qiblah﴾, meaning: a mosque.

It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: God, exalted is He, commanded them to face the Ka'bah. Some said: they feared to display the prayer, so God, exalted is He, commanded them to establish the prayer in their houses. As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾, its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 88:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And Moses said, "Our Lord, indeed You have given Pharaoh and his chiefs﴾ — the verse. His words: ﴿adornment and wealth in the life of this world﴾. It has been said in the tafsir that it extended from the fortress of Egypt to al-'Arish, to near Abyssinia, with mines of gold, silver, ruby and chrysolite. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿adornment and wealth in the life of this world, our Lord, so that they may lead astray from Your way﴾. The people of tafsir said: this "lam" is the lam of ṣayrūra (the lam of outcome), and it is said: it is the lam of 'āqiba (the lam of consequence). This is like the words of the poet:

(And for death is what the mother bears...)

Since the outcome of their affair was misguidance and disbelief, He said: ﴿so that they may lead astray from Your way﴾. ﴿Our Lord, obliterate their wealth﴾. Ṭams (obliteration): changing the form of a thing; it has been said: it is effacement and the erasing of a trace. Qatada said: their wealth, their crops, their plants and their jewels all became stones. In some narrations: their slaves and their female slaves became stones.

And His words: ﴿and harden their hearts﴾. Mujahid said: with misguidance. As-Suddi said: make them die upon disbelief.

And His words: ﴿so that they will not believe until they see the painful punishment﴾. It has been said: this is in the sense of supplication, as if he said: "so let them not believe until they see the painful punishment." It has also been said: its meaning is that of a report.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 89:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿He said: "Your supplication has been answered."﴾ In Surat al-Qasas it is mentioned that the interval between the supplication of Musa and its answer was forty years, and likewise the interval between the supplication of Ya'qub and its answer was forty years. If someone says: "The one who supplicated was Musa, yet He said: ﴿Your supplication has been answered,﴾" 

The transmitted answer is: Musa was supplicating while Harun was saying "Amin," and the saying of "Amin" is itself a supplication, for the meaning of "Amin" is: "O Allah, answer."

His saying: ﴿So go straight﴾ means: upon obedience and the religion. His saying: ﴿and do not follow the path of those who do not know﴾ has a clear meaning.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 10, verse 90:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We brought the Children of Israel across the sea﴾, the verse. Its meaning: We made the Children of Israel pass over the sea. And His saying: ﴿Then Pharaoh followed them with his hosts﴾. Al-Asma'i (al-Asma'i) said: it is said "atba'ahu" when one travels in his footsteps, and "atba'ahu" when one overtakes him and catches up with him. And His saying: ﴿in rebellion and enmity﴾ — injustice and transgression. It has been recited as "'adwan" and "'udwan", and the meaning is one.

And His saying: ﴿until, when drowning overtook him﴾ — meaning: until, when the water covered him and his destruction drew near. ﴿He said: I believe that there is no god except the One in whom the Children of Israel believe﴾ — meaning: I believe in the God in whom the Children of Israel believe. ﴿And I am among the Muslims﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 91:

And His saying: ﴿Now? And you had disobeyed before and were among the corrupters﴾ — in the (chapter on) al-Qasas (stories): that Jibril was standing when he said this statement, and he said to him: "Now? And you had disobeyed before and were among the corrupters." He said this statement by the command of Allah, the Exalted: "Now? And you had disobeyed."

And Yusuf ibn Mihran narrated, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that Jibril, peace be upon him, said: "O Muhammad, if you had seen me as I took from the side of the sea and pushed it into the mouth of Pharaoh, fearing that mercy would reach him." And in another narration: "That Jibril said: O Muhammad, I have never hated any of Allah's creatures as much as I hated Pharaoh when he said to his people: ﴿I do not know for you any god other than Me﴾. Then when he said what he said, as he drowned, I began pushing the mud into his mouth, lest he say: there is no god but Allah." And in another narration: "lest he be mentioned (with mercy), for fear that Allah would forgive him."

Abu 'Isa said: And the hadith is sound in general.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 92:

And His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿So today We shall save you in your body⁠﴾ — in the sea. It was recited as "nunahhika" (we shall remove you) with a ḥāʾ, from al-tanḥiya (removal), whereas the well-known reading has a jīm, meaning: We shall cast you upon a najwa (elevated ground) of the earth. Al-najwa: the elevated place.

In the narratives it is related that when Pharaoh drowned, the Children of Israel said: "He is too grand to drown." So they did not believe Moses that he had drowned. Therefore God, the Exalted, commanded the water until it threw him onto his face. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿We shall save you in your body⁠﴾. As for His saying: ﴿in your body⁠﴾, there are two opinions:

The first: in your armour. He had a famous coat of mail of pearls, inlaid with jewels, and they saw him in his armour and believed.

The second opinion: "in your body" means: in a body with no spirit in it.

As for His saying: ﴿So that it may be a sign for those who come after you⁠﴾, meaning: a lesson. And His saying: ﴿Indeed, many of the people are heedless of Our signs⁠﴾, its meaning is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 93:

And His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿And We certainly settled the Children of Israel in a good dwelling-place﴾, meaning: We settled the Children of Israel in a dwelling-place of truth, that is, We settled the Children of Israel in abodes of truth. It has been said: these dwellings were Egypt. It has also been said: they were Syria (al-Sham). His saying ﴿a dwelling-place of truth﴾ means: by their truthfulness and their faith. His saying ﴿and We provided them with good things﴾ is well known. His saying ﴿And they did not differ until knowledge had come to them﴾ means: the Torah, for they differed after the Torah was revealed and after Musa had departed, with severe differing. Then He said: ﴿Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein they used to differ﴾. The meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 94:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿If you are in doubt about what We have sent down to you﴾. There is a well-known question concerning this verse, namely: He said, ﴿If you are in doubt﴾; how is it permissible for the Messenger to be in doubt, such that He says to him, "If you are in doubt"?

The answer is given in several ways. The first: the address is directed to him, but what is meant is his people. This is like His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women﴾, and there are many similar examples.

Some of them said: its implied meaning is: "If you are in doubt, O doubter, then ask those who read the Book before you."

The second aspect: the meaning of the verse is: "You were not in doubt."

His saying: ﴿So ask those who read the Book before you﴾ is an addition for reinforcement. "Those who read the Book" are those among the Jews who embraced Islam, such as ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam (ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam) and Ibn Yamin (Ibn Yamin) and others.

The third aspect: this is in accordance with the customary speech of the Arabs, for a man says to his son, "Do such-and-such if you are my son," and this does not imply doubt; and likewise he says to his servant, "Feed me if you are my slave," and it does not imply doubt.

His saying: ﴿So ask those who read the Book before you﴾, meaning: order them ﴿So ask those who read the Book before you. Certainly the truth has come to you from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters﴾, that is, among the skeptics; and its meaning is: remain upon the certainty in which you are.

The first aspect is the choice of al-Zajjaj (al-Zajjaj) and others among the scholars of meanings (ahl al-maʿani).
Al-Sam'ani's words: "And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And do not be among those who deny the signs of Allah﴾ to the end of the verse, its meaning is apparent."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verses 96–97:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has been justified﴾ means: the punishment of your Lord has become obligatory for them.

It is also said: the meaning of "the word" is His saying, exalted is He: "These are for Paradise and I do not mind, and these are for the Fire and I do not mind," as has been related in the reports.

And His saying: ﴿They will not believe, even if every sign should come to them, until they see the painful punishment﴾ means: faith comes only at the time of the violent punishment (al-ba's, "the time of severity").

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verses 96–97:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has been justified﴾ means: the punishment of your Lord has become obligatory for them.

It is also said: the meaning of "the word" is His saying, exalted is He: "These are for Paradise and I do not mind, and these are for the Fire and I do not mind," as has been related in the reports.

And His saying: ﴿They will not believe, even if every sign should come to them, until they see the painful punishment﴾ means: faith comes only at the time of the violent punishment (al-ba's, "the time of severity").

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 98:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Why was there not a town that believed so that its faith would benefit it, except the people of Yunus?﴾ Its meaning: there was not a town that believed—that is, the people of a town that believed—so that their faith would benefit them, except the people of Yunus (Yunus). This faith was at the descent of the punishment. What is related in the narratives is that Yunus—may the blessings of God be upon him—warned his people of the punishment and left them. When they saw the punishment, like fires in the sky, they went out from their town into the desert, separated the children from their mothers, the livestock and the young animals, and cried out to God Most High with one single outcry. God removed the punishment from them after they had seen it with their own eyes, and He did not do this for anyone other than them. This is the meaning of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿except the people of Yunus; when they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world and gave them enjoyment for a time﴾, that is, until a known term.

In some tafsirs it is said that the supplication with which the people of Yunus called out was: "O Living, when there is no living; O Living, O Giver of life to the dead; O Living, there is no god but You."

There is disagreement as to whether they saw the punishment with their own eyes or only saw a sign of the punishment. Most scholars hold that they saw the punishment with their own eyes. Qatadah said: the punishment drew near to them until it became between them and the punishment about a mile's distance. Others said: they saw a sign of the punishment, but did not see the punishment itself.

The first view is more sound, based on His saying: ﴿We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world﴾, and removal occurs only after the punishment has befallen or drawn very near. If someone asks: how was their faith accepted at the moment of seeing [the punishment], while the faith of others was not accepted, and He said elsewhere: ﴿who believe in the unseen﴾, which shows that accepted faith is faith in the unseen?

The answer: the people of Yunus were excepted from this general rule by the explicit text of the Qur'an, and God does what He wills, and He is not to be questioned about what He does. Al-Khalil and Sibawayh held that the exception here is disjunctive (munqati'), and the meaning of the verse is: "But the people of Yunus, when they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world."

It is related from Ali—may God be pleased with him—that he said: Caution does not avert decree, but supplication averts decree; for God Most High removed the punishment from the people of Yunus through supplication. It is also related from Ali that he said: the removal of the punishment was on the day of Ashura.

It has been said, regarding the construction of the beginning of the verse: "Why was there not" a town that believed at the time when its faith would benefit it; but the people of Yunus, when they believed, We removed the punishment from them. And "town" means the people of a town. It has also been said: the name of that town was Nineveh, from the lands of al-Jazira.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 99:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if your Lord had willed, those on earth would have believed, all of them together﴾. In the verse there is a refutation of the Qadariyyah (the Qadariyya, an early theological school that affirmed human power over action), for He, exalted is He, informed that He did not will the faith of all people, whereas they hold that He willed the faith of all people. And His saying: ﴿Would you then compel the people until they become believers?﴾ This is a consolation to the Prophet (ﷺ): that if I had willed, I would have compelled them to faith, but I did not will it; so you too should not wish to compel them to faith.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 100:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And it is not for a soul to believe except by the permission of Allah﴾. ʿAṭāʾ said: "Except by the enabling (tawfīq) of Allah." Others said: "Except by the knowledge (ʿilm) of Allah." It has also been said: "Except by Allah's releasing that (i.e., permitting it) by removing the impediments." This is like His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And it is not for a soul to die except by the permission of Allah﴾. Some of them said: "By the permission of Allah" means: by His decree, His determination and His judgment. All of these meanings are correct.

As for His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And He places the defilement upon those who do not reason﴾. Al-Farrāʾ said: "Al-rijs (defilement) has the meaning of ar-rijz, and ar-rijz is the punishment." Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "Indeed, ar-rijs is the wrath (al-sakhaṭ)." It has also been said: "It is the sin (al-ithm)." It has also been said: "It is the destruction (al-halāk)."

As for His saying: ﴿upon those who do not reason﴾, its meaning is: they do not believe. It has also been said: the meaning of His saying: ﴿who do not reason﴾ is: who do not reason about Allah's command and His prohibition.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 101:

His saying: ﴿Say: Look at what is in the heavens and the earth﴾. Its meaning: Say: Look at what is in the heavens and the earth of proofs, lessons and arguments.

And His saying: ﴿But signs and warnings avail not a people who do not believe﴾. This is concerning specific people whom God, exalted is He, knew would not believe even if they looked at the signs.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 102:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Then are they waiting for anything but the like of the days of those who passed away before them?﴾ Al-intizar (waiting) is the remaining steadfast in anticipation of a matter. And His words: ﴿but the like of the days of those who passed away before them﴾ mean: the like of the days of destruction that befell those who passed away before them, from the nations that denied (their messengers). His words: ﴿Say, "Then wait; indeed I am with you among those who wait."﴾ are clear in meaning.

Divine words: ﴿Then We save Our messengers and those who believe﴾. His saying "nunajji" (we save) is in the future form but carries the meaning of the past; its meaning is: We saved Our messengers and those who believed. His saying ﴿Thus, it is a truth upon Us that We save the believers﴾ means: Muhammad (ﷺ) and his companions.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 104:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: O people, if you are in doubt about my religion﴾. If someone asks: How can He say, "if you are in doubt about my religion," when they were holding the falsehood of what he brought to be certain (ʿalā baṣīrah)?

The answer: There were indeed among them people who were doubtful, so the intended meaning of the verse is those people.

The second answer: when they saw the signs, they became agitated and doubted their own affair and the affair of the Prophet.

His saying: ﴿So I do not worship those whom you worship besides God, but I worship God, who causes you to die﴾. The meaning is apparent. If someone asks: What is the meaning of His saying, "If you are in doubt about my religion, then I do not worship those whom you worship besides God," when he does not worship those besides God whether they doubted or did not doubt? And what is the meaning of His saying, "but I worship God, who causes you to die," and why was death specifically mentioned?

The answer: As for the first, its meaning is: if you are in doubt, then I am not in doubt, and I worship none but God, with certainty and clear insight. As for the mention of death in His saying, "who causes you to die," it carries the sense of a threat, for punishment befalls the disbeliever until death overtakes him.

﴿And I have been commanded to be among the believers﴾, that is: among the sincere (al-mukhlisīn).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 10, verse 105:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And that I should set my face toward the religion, as a ḥanīf﴾. Its meaning: "And I have been commanded to be upright before God in the religion, sincerely devoted." It is also said that its meaning is: "Be steadfast in the religion which you have been commanded, with your face (turned toward it)." His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿ḥanīfan﴾ (ḥanīf, one who turns away from falsehood toward the true religion) has already been explained earlier. It is also said that the verse concerns facing the qiblah, which is the Ka'bah, and it is in the same sense as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque﴾. As for His saying: ﴿And do not be among the polytheists﴾, its meaning is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 106:

The Most High said: ﴿And do not call upon, besides Allah, that which can neither benefit you nor harm you﴾. Du'a' (supplication, calling upon) has two meanings. The first: in the sense of calling out, as when you say, "O Zayd," and "O 'Amr." The second: in the sense of asking and requesting.

His words ﴿that which can neither benefit you nor harm you﴾ mean: it cannot benefit you if you call upon it, and it cannot harm you if you abandon its supplication. And His words ﴿For if you do, then indeed you would be among the wrongdoers﴾ mean: among those who place supplication in other than its proper place.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 107:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if Allah touches you with harm, there is none to remove it except Him﴾. Its meaning: if Allah afflicts you with harm. Harm (ḍurr) is fear, sickness, hunger and the like.

His saying: ﴿there is none to remove it except Him﴾, i.e., there is none to remove that harm except Allah.

His saying: ﴿And if He intends you good﴾, i.e., if He afflicts you with good. Good (khayr) is fertility, abundance, well-being and the like.

His saying: ﴿there is no repeller of His bounty﴾, i.e., there is no one who can prevent His bounty.

His saying: ﴿He gives it to whom He wills of His servants, and He is the Oft-Forgiving, the Most Merciful﴾: its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 108:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Say, "O mankind, the truth has certainly come to you from your Lord."﴾ Al-haqq (the truth) here is that by which a person is saved, and its opposite is al-batil (falsehood), which is that by which a person is destroyed. It is said that its meaning is Islam. It is said that its meaning is the Qur'an.

His words: ﴿So whoever is guided is only guided for [the benefit of] himself﴾, meaning: he takes precaution for his own self. ﴿And whoever strays only strays against it [i.e., to its detriment]﴾, meaning: whoever disbelieves and abandons faith, then its consequence and its misguidance fall upon him.

His words: ﴿And I am not over you a manager.﴾ That is: not a controller (musallat). Its meaning is that you will be questioned about your deeds, and I will not be questioned about your deeds, just as one who has been entrusted with a matter is questioned about it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 10, verse 109:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And follow what is revealed to you﴾. Al-wahy (revelation, inspiration): the casting of something into a person's heart in secret. His saying: ﴿and be patient﴾. Al-sabr (patience): swallowing bitterness by refraining from what one desires, in expectation of what is beloved in the outcome. Among the things that help a person to be patient is his knowledge of the reality of the matter, what reward he will obtain, and his trust in the promise of God, exalted is He. His saying: ﴿until God judges﴾, that is, until God decides. ﴿And He is the best of judges﴾, that is, the best of those who decide.
